 Utah Jazz guard Darryn Peterson made his much-awaited debut in the NBA on Wednesday, fulfilling a lifelong dream, with his family and friends being proud of how far he has come.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement However, Memphis Grizzlies guard Ty Jerome decided to gate-crash the party.
 Peterson, the No. 2 pick in this year's draft, was slapped with a reality check, as he was embarrassed by Jerome—again and again. It probably felt like being in a nightmare ad nauseam. The Grizzlies blew out the Jazz, 123-103, at FedExForum.
 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) 
 Jerome dropped a career-high 45 points on top of seven rebounds and six assists. He shot 17-of-25 from the field, including 5-of-10 from long range.
 Peterson, meanwhile, had nine points on 3-of-7 shooting from the floor, four rebounds, and three assists.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Fans made the same joke after the 19-year-old rookie was destroyed by the 29-year-old journeyman.
 "Darryn Peterson's gonna be on a podcast in eight years talking about Ty Jerome as his welcome-to-the-league moment," said @stillreggie_.
 "(Jerome) gave Darryn Peterson a warm welcome to the league, LMAO," added @EB3TV_.
 "In 10 years, they're gonna ask Darryn Peterson what was his welcome-to-the-NBA moment, and this would be his answer," echoed @Love4ADolla.
 "A year and a half from now, one of these NBA player podcasts will ask Darryn Peterson what his welcome-to-the-league moment was, and watch him say 'Ty Jerome dropped 45 on opening night,'" wrote @kikuua.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Darryn Peterson's welcome-to-the-NBA moment being Ty Jerome is gonna be a funny story to tell," commented @AaronSpencer__.
 Click Here to Subscribe In the meantime, it is hard for Peterson to laugh.
 But he will surely learn from the experience, and getting knocked down early could be a blessing in disguise.
 The Jazz will host the New Orleans Pelicans on Friday.
